papers.title: Effect of Scanning Speed on the Microstructure and Properties of Co-Cu-Ti Coatings by Laser Cladding
papers.abstract: Co-Cu-Ti composite coatings were fabricated on Ti6Al4V substrates by laser cladding. The Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation–Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution methodology was employed to determine the optimal parameters. The effect of varying the scanning speed, a critical parameter, was investigated to evaluate its influence on the coating’s microstructure and performance. The phase composition of the coatings comprises Co-Ti phases and Cu-Ti phases. The microhardness and wear resistance of the coatings initially increase as the scanning speed rises, reaching a peak before subsequently declining. The predominant wear mechanisms of the coatings are abrasive wear, with minor contributions from adhesive wear and fatigue wear. The wear resistance of the coating is superior to that of the TC4 substrate, primarily due to the synergistic enhancement from the strengthening effect of the Co-Ti phase and the lubricating effect of the Cu-Ti phase. The composite coatings fabricated at a scanning speed of 3 mm/s exhibited superior properties. Specifically, the microhardness measures 788 HV0.2, the coefficient of friction is approximately 0.57, and the wear cross-sectional area is 3.57 × 10−9 mm2. At this speed, these two effects achieve an optimal balance, making it the best process parameter for wear resistance.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是Ti6Al4V基体上Co-Cu-Ti涂层的激光熔覆，而非Ti-6Al-4V本身的力学或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: The paper is about laser cladding of Co-Cu-Ti coatings on Ti6Al4V substrate, focusing on coating microstructure and wear resistance, not on mechanical or fatigue properties of the Ti-6Al-4V itself.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光熔覆Co-Cu-Ti涂层在Ti6Al4V基体上的最佳工艺参数。
summary_zh.method: 使用CRITIC-TOPSIS方法优化参数，研究扫描速度对涂层显微组织和性能的影响。
summary_zh.result: 扫描速度3 mm/s时涂层性能最优，显微硬度788 HV0.2，摩擦系数约0.57。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微硬度测试、摩擦磨损实验验证涂层性能。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to optimize laser cladding parameters for Co-Cu-Ti coatings on Ti6Al4V substrates to achieve superior wear resistance.
summary_en.method: The CRITIC-TOPSIS methodology was used to determine optimal parameters, and the effect of scanning speed on coating microstructure and performance was investigated.
summary_en.result: A scanning speed of 3 mm/s yielded the best coating performance with a microhardness of 788 HV0.2 and a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.57.
summary_en.validation: The coating performance was validated through microhardness measurements and wear tests, demonstrating abrasive wear as the dominant mechanism.

papers.title: Microstructural, mechanical and biocompatibility of Zr/Ti6Al4V alloy fabricated by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Titanium alloys are extensively employed as biomaterials for orthopedic and dental implants owing to their intrinsic corrosion resistance, high specific strength, and biocompatibility. In this study, Zr/Ti–6Al–4V (TC4) alloys containing up to 4 wt% Zr were fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM). Microstructural analysis revealed that Zr additions refined the microstructure and acted as a β-phase stabilizer, thereby suppressing the formation of acicular α′ martensite. Consequently, the 4 wt% Zr/TC4 alloy exhibited enhanced mechanical performance, achieving an ultimate tensile strength of 1482 MPa and a Vickers hardness of 461 HV, corresponding to increases of 55 % and 25 %, respectively, relative to TC4. Electrochemical measurements in Hanks’ solution demonstrated a positive shift in corrosion potential to −0.504 V and a reduction in corrosion current density to 3.106 × 10 −7 A cm −2 , indicating improved corrosion resistance. In vitro assays using Saos-2 cells showed >200 % higher adhesion after 24 h on the 4 wt% Zr/TC4 surface compared with TC4, evidencing enhanced cytocompatibility. Collectively, modest Zr alloying improves strength, corrosion resistance, and cytocompatibility of SLM-fabricated TC4, highlighting its potential for next-generation load-bearing biomedical implants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文研究了添加Zr的SLM Ti-6Al-4V合金的力学性能，但未涉及疲劳性能，方向为Ti-6Al-4V基础力学与疲劳，因此相关但非核心。
llm.why_not_core: No fatigue testing or S-N data; the paper primarily focuses on alloy modification and biocompatibility, not on fatigue life or crack growth.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过添加Zr改善SLM Ti-6Al-4V的力学性能、耐腐蚀性和生物相容性。
summary_zh.method: 利用SLM制备不同Zr含量的Ti-6Al-4V合金，进行微观表征、力学测试和电化学测量。
summary_zh.result: 4%Zr合金抗拉强度达1482 MPa，硬度461 HV，腐蚀电位正移，细胞粘附提高200%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸、硬度、电化学和细胞实验验证性能提升。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility of SLM-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V through Zr alloying.
summary_en.method: Zr/Ti-6Al-4V alloys with up to 4 wt% Zr were fabricated via selective laser melting, followed by microstructural, mechanical, electrochemical, and in vitro cell assays.
summary_en.result: The 4 wt% Zr alloy achieved an ultimate tensile strength of 1482 MPa, Vickers hardness of 461 HV, improved corrosion resistance, and a 200% increase in cell adhesion.
summary_en.validation: Tensile testing, hardness indentation, electrochemical polarization, and Saos-2 cell adhesion assays provided experimental validation.
